citation.title: A Framework for Random-Effects ROC Analysis: Biases with the Bootstrap and Other Variance Estimators
citation.authors: Gallas, B. D.; Bandos, A.; Samuelson, F. W.; Wagner, R. F.

topic: Variance estimation for the reader-averaged nonparametric AUC in multi-reader multi-case medical-imaging ROC studies. The paper analyses bias in the three-way bootstrap, DBM, BWC and one-shot U-statistic estimators.
own_question: How biased are the bootstrap and related estimators of the variance of the reader-averaged AUC under crossed random readers and random cases?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors develop a success-moment framework (Table 1–2) and give closed-form bias expressions in Appendices B–D. They test the estimators on a simulated 16x16-pixel lesion-detection task with linear-classifier readers (27 configurations, 10,000 Monte Carlo trials). They also apply the estimators to one clinical CAD mammography reader study. No fusion data, CES data, time series or nowcasting appear.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. The paper has no temporal inputs or targets and no report-arrival timing.
validation_if_relevant: Simulation plus one reused clinical dataset. This applies to medical ROC analysis only.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite this paper as support for any plasma, CES, BES or ECEI claim.
Do not treat its three-way bootstrap bias as demonstrated for our temporal or chord data.
Do not infer that we used ROC/AUC or MRMC designs.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The domain and estimand (ROC AUC variance across readers and cases) do not match our causal regression nowcasting task. Its bootstrap-bias results come from crossed independent populations, not dependent fusion time series. A general resampling-uncertainty citation would be peripheral at best and could mislead readers.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
